clue.text: Supposed party, but not one was in the van

indicators.note: 'but not' tells us to drop one piece from the word just given for party

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
I is the Roman numeral for one
to be in the van (vanguard) is to be at the front, so led

explanation.surface: Someone claims a party was underway, though nobody was actually in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the van' means in the vanguard, at the front, not inside a vehicle; 'but not' removes the I from the word for party.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something called by a name it may not deserve: an alleged or purported thing.

clue.text: See 3
Still hangs out to dry reason why 9 10?

definitions.meaning: remains pegged up on a washing cord, verb plus phrase
9 and 10 read together say a railway service is delayed; this is a classic British excuse for that

explanation.surface: Washing is still pegged out, and that somehow explains why the trains are delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads 'leaves' as the verb 'remains'. Autumn foliage on the tracks is a famous British rail excuse; 9 and 10 together give the phrase about trains being delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallen foliage on tracks causes wheel slip, a well-known cause of delays on British railways.

clue.text: See 22 across
Conclusion of anonymous alcoholic — one going dotty?

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here taken from anonymous

parts.note: a tippler is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: An anonymous alcoholic's story ends with someone losing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going dotty' suggests madness, but stippling is painting with dots.
explanation.definitionFit: A stippler is an artist who applies paint in small dots, so cryptically one going dotty.

clue.text: Group, by word of introduction into the mob, moving clumsily

indicators.note: 'into' says the first pieces are placed inside the word for the mob

parts.note: a gang is a mob or band of criminals
a lump is a mass or group of things
hi is a greeting used when meeting someone

explanation.surface: A group greeted by a mob shuffles off awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link joining the two inserted pieces; 'mob' looks like the subject being moved, but it is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Galumphing means moving in a heavy, clumsy, noisy way, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Skim book containing name for another book

indicators.note: 'containing' says the shortened word holds the next piece inside it
to skim is to take off the top, so the first letter goes from the word for a book

parts.note: a manual is a handbook

explanation.surface: Someone flicks through a book that mentions another title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skim' looks like quick reading, but it means remove the top: MANUAL loses M to give ANUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published yearly, often a children's gift book at Christmas.

clue.text: Look more attractive with a flowering plant

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
nicer means more pleasant or attractive

explanation.surface: Someone looks prettier holding a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonicera is the botanical genus of honeysuckle, a climbing plant with fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Work out the following group

definitions.meaning: to exercise or practise in order to get fit
a retinue or procession following someone

explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to get in shape by drill, and a retinue is a line of followers behind someone.

clue.text: Gone, though still to come?

definitions.meaning: dead, departed, as in a recently deceased person

explanation.walkthrough: The same word means dead and also behind schedule; 'though' joins the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone deceased and also something that has not yet turned up on time.

clue.text: Fully provocative book on drugs issued in recession by America

parts.note: vol is short for volume, a book
up can mean high, under the influence

indicators.note: recession means going backwards, so the word for issued is turned round

parts.note: out means published or issued
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A racy book about drug use was published in reverse by an American press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' looks economic but signals reversal: OUT becomes TUO.
explanation.definitionFit: Voluptuous describes a full-figured, sexually alluring body, so curvaceous and provocative.

clue.text: Sacha Baron Cohen man takes partners' orders

parts.note: Ali G is a comic character created by Sacha Baron Cohen
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: A comedian's character takes his friends' instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To line things up in a row is to put them in order, so the verb arranges or orders.

clue.text: Outskirts of Derby creating new rural development

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made afresh in another arrangement
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Building on the edge of Derby is creating a new estate in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: DY from Derby joins CREATING and all ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden city is a planned town with green spaces, such as Letchworth, built to blend town and countryside.

clue.text: Fatty pudding

definitions.meaning: a British steamed suet pudding rolled with jam

explanation.walkthrough: The pudding is a suet sponge spread with jam and rolled up, a British school-dinner staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a chubby person and also a rolled jam suet dessert.

clue.text: Deal with name before this?

definitions.meaning: to tackle a problem or speak to someone
on an envelope the recipient's name is written above where they live

explanation.definitionFit: To tackle an issue is to address it, and the postal details follow the name on a letter.

clue.text: Break china up with six Chinamen, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: china means crockery, pots
in cricket an over is six balls, and a chinaman is one kind of spin delivery

explanation.surface: Breaking crockery alongside six men from China.
explanation.walkthrough: A chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spin ball in cricket; six balls make an over. 'up' turns POTS into STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, a pause before continuing.

clue.text: Possibly a feature

definitions.meaning: the word a is an example of the indefinite one in grammar
a piece written for a newspaper or magazine

explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a grammatical determiner of the indefinite kind, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'a' the indefinite one of these, and a newspaper feature is a written piece of this name.

clue.text: Fifty at work at school

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
someone at work is earning a wage

explanation.surface: Fifty people are working at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at school are engaged in study, acquiring knowledge.

clue.text: Answers found in the laboratory?

definitions.meaning: glass vessels with long bent necks used for distilling

explanation.definitionFit: The word means witty replies and also distilling flasks used by chemists.

clue.text: Having left one's love, this setter feeling so?

parts.note: taken as one plus 's, giving ONES
love is zero in tennis, O
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Having lost his love, the setter wonders whether he feels this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'feeling' are links in the wordplay reading; 'so' refers to the state the whole sentence describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling forlorn and solitary after a parting would feel this way, isolated and sad.

clue.text: See 26
12 could be the reason why 9 10

definitions.meaning: the entry at 12 is the word for an alert jumbled, a botched spelling of it
a common cause given for delayed railway services

explanation.walkthrough: ALIGNS (12) is a failed attempt at spelling the word for an alert, cryptically a failure of that word. 9 and 10 give trains being delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken railway warning light is a standard reason for delayed services in Britain.

clue.text: One arranges to get setting up of bank under way?

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for bank, reversed, sits below the word for way

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up means reading the word upwards

parts.note: to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for a riverbank to be raised once work is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a river edge but means rely, as in bank on; turned upwards it gives YLER under ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A styler shapes or arranges something, typically hair, so one who arranges.

clue.text: Thinking spy erroneously caught, very good to conceal own goal

indicators.note: erroneously says the three letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: 'to conceal' says the word for very good hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: holy means saintly, very good
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A spy is wrongly caught, and a decent person covers up a football blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very good' as a saintly sense is a crossword favourite; 'own goal' is football, not psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychology is the study of the mind and its mental processes, so of thinking.

clue.text: See 26
Church sees drink to its end

parts.note: kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur
its end means the last letter of the word drink itself

explanation.surface: A church sees someone drinking to the bitter end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link meaning followed by; 'its end' points back at the clue word drink, whose last letter is K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirk is the Scottish word for a church.

clue.text: See 3
Wind known with fog and others to form reason why 9 10?

indicators.note: to form says the letters of the four words are shaped into a new phrase

explanation.surface: Wind, fog and other weather combine to cause something.
explanation.walkthrough: WIND, KNOWN, FOG and OTHERS give eighteen letters rearranged; 'with' and 'and' are links. This was a famous 1991 British Rail excuse, as 9 and 10 give trains being delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: British Rail infamously blamed delays on a particular powdery type of winter precipitation, a notorious excuse.
